text: We can reach that great goal of full employment.
explanation: 'We can reach that great goal of full employment' — 'great' is a weak evaluative flourish attached to an economic policy goal. It does not invoke ethical concepts, rights, or desert, so it remains an economic aspiration.

text: Every element of America's homeland security plan is critical, because the terrorists are ruthless and resourceful - and we know they are preparing to attack us again.
explanation: Characterizing terrorists as 'ruthless' is an explicitly evaluative moral judgment of character (lacking mercy/compassion), going beyond a purely technical threat assessment. This fits the codebook's allowance for moralized character evaluations (cf. 'corruption' as an ethical concept marker), though I note some ambiguity since the sentence primarily justifies a security plan.

text: o  each minister should prepare and publish a statement of the skills and roles sought for each board.
explanation: A governance procedure (ministers publishing statements of skills and roles sought for boards) — purely administrative.

text: We have had an unprecedented 16 years of continuous economic expansion.
explanation: A factual/economic claim about 16 years of continuous expansion. No normative content.

text: We want young New Zealanders to be able to join KiwiSaver and stay in it for their working lives.
explanation: A programmatic aspiration for young people to join and stay in KiwiSaver — savings policy without moral framing.

text: • It has been four years since the Maori Commercial Settlement Act was passed, and most iwi are yet to receive any form of settlement from the Crown.
explanation: Notes factually that most iwi have not yet received settlements four years after the Act. While it implies a grievance, it contains no explicit moralized or evaluative language (no 'unjust', 'deserve', 'obligation'), so under the codebook's requirement for explicit normative terminology it is coded 0.

text: Those policies have placed the federal government in the driver’s seat,
explanation: Metaphorical description of policy effects ('federal government in the driver's seat') with no ethical or normative content.

text: This has resulted in increased pressure in the health system and failed outcomes for healthcare staff, patients and the public.
explanation: 'Failed outcomes' is a performance/technical evaluation of the health system, not a moral judgment. Criticism of policy effectiveness without ethical framing.

text: •  More than two in every three New  Zealanders  does unpaid work outside their  own households.
explanation: A descriptive statistic about unpaid work prevalence. No normative language.

text: ACARA will work with States and Territories to ensure the Cadetships contribute towards state based senior awards, in the same way as other approved subjects under the National Curriculum
explanation: Administrative detail about ACARA coordinating cadetship recognition within the National Curriculum. Purely procedural.

text: That’s why President Obama and Democrats in Congress have enacted infrastructure investments that will
explanation: Descriptive statement about infrastructure investments enacted by Obama and Democrats — programmatic/fiscal content.

text: Increased funding for early childhood education by $550 million, or 40 per cent, since 2008.
explanation: Fiscal spending claim ($550 million increase in early childhood education funding). Excluded by the negative clarification on fiscal spending descriptions.

text: Labor’s Infrastructure Australia is a secretive organisation.
explanation: Calling Infrastructure Australia 'a secretive organisation' deploys explicitly evaluative language condemning a breach of the governance norm of transparency/openness. This goes beyond pure description into moralized criticism (analogous to 'corruption' as an ethical concept marker), though I acknowledge it is a thin, single-adjective case.

text: South Island domestic and industrial users will have their price discounted.
explanation: A price discount commitment for South Island users — purely programmatic/economic.

text: Labor has done little to educate the public on the benefits of cleaner fuels.
explanation: Criticism that Labor 'has done little to educate the public on the benefits of cleaner fuels' is a performance critique of policy implementation, lacking moral or ethical vocabulary.

text: In 1997, a single person on the average industrial wage paid 22% of their income in income tax.
explanation: A factual statistic about income tax rates in 1997. No normative content.

text: Together we're the co-leaders of the Green party
explanation: A descriptive biographical statement about party co-leadership. No moral language.

text: without allowing emissions from aviation to undermine our goal of a zero-carbon Britain by 2050.
explanation: States an environmental policy constraint (aviation emissions vs. zero-carbon goal) in technical terms. Environmental goals alone do not constitute moral rhetoric per the negative clarification.

text: The development of an ‘alternative growth pole’ along the Atlantic Corridor will be pursued.
explanation: A regional development commitment ('alternative growth pole' along the Atlantic Corridor) — purely programmatic.

text: This will be underpinned by new rights for patients.
explanation: 'New rights for patients' frames health policy in terms of rights — entitlements patients are owed — which the codebook's definition links to moral rhetoric (rights and what individuals deserve). Thin, but the rights language is explicitly normative rather than purely administrative.

text: Current investment in developing and protecting the Australian farm sector does not recognise the large contribution farmers make to our economy.
explanation: Argues current investment 'does not recognise the large contribution farmers make to our economy'. This is an economic-contribution justification for investment, a utilitarian argument rather than an appeal to fairness or desert.

text: We recognize that adoption costs can be high and in some cases prohibitive for families.
explanation: Acknowledges that adoption costs can be prohibitive for families — a descriptive statement of a practical/financial problem without moral or evaluative terminology.

text: We will increase access to the arts for young people, particularly those of disadvantaged backgrounds,
explanation: A commitment to increase arts access, particularly for those of 'disadvantaged backgrounds'. Per the negative clarification, targeting a positive outcome for a disadvantaged group without explicitly moralized language (no 'deserve', 'fairness', 'justice') is a generic social policy commitment and is coded 0.

text: Direct this new spending to health, education, and a few carefully targeted initiatives.
explanation: A purely programmatic directive on where to allocate new spending (health, education, targeted initiatives). Per the negative clarification, fiscal spending commitments without explicitly moralized or evaluative language are coded 0.

text: The Green Party is committed to bringing rail services into public ownership and control.
explanation: A generic policy commitment to bring rail services into public ownership. No ethical concepts, virtues, or moral-duty language is deployed; it is an administrative/ownership proposal.

text: provide direct and meaningful support to land managers in delivering ecoservices; | and
explanation: Technical agri-environmental policy support for land managers delivering ecoservices. 'Meaningful support' is not an ethical concept, and there is no normative or moral framing.

text: and providing other services as required, thus contributing to Ireland’s political and economic well being.
explanation: Administrative description of services contributing to Ireland's political and economic well-being. No moralized terminology; purely descriptive of institutional functions.

text: • Conflicting roles and responsibilities.
explanation: A descriptive bullet noting conflicting roles and responsibilities. Contains no normative, evaluative, or ethical language whatsoever.

text: An SNP government will strive to ensure that Scotland becomes a world leader in securing a sustainable environment
explanation: An aspirational commitment to environmental leadership and sustainability. Per the negative clarification, environmental aims stated without explicitly moralized or evaluative ethical language are excluded.

text: With the investment that we are promising in hospital buildings,
explanation: A fragment about promised investment in hospital buildings — purely infrastructural/programmatic with no moral framing.

text: The question that should still be asked of Labor is:
explanation: A rhetorical lead-in question directed at Labor with no substantive content or moral terminology.

text: And with new laws to crack down on domestic violence,
explanation: Announces new laws to crack down on domestic violence. This is an instrumental law-and-order policy statement; it does not explicitly deploy ethical or moralized language (e.g., justice, dignity, desert), so per the negative clarification it is coded 0 despite the socially beneficial aim.

text: Fine Gael will support the on-going nationwide roll out of the “Food Dudes” Fruit and Vegetable Promotion programme to all primary schools in Ireland.
explanation: A programmatic commitment to roll out a fruit and vegetable promotion programme in schools. No normative or ethical framing.

text: Every board shall publish before March of each year an annual report on  its own activities as opposed to the wider work of the state body.
explanation: An administrative transparency requirement (annual reports by boards). Procedural in nature with no moral vocabulary.

text: In particular, as we expand access to talking therapies we expect many more people to recover and be able to seek work again.
explanation: Health policy (talking therapies) justified on utilitarian grounds — recovery and return to work. The framing is economic/functional, not ethical.

text: and free up  resources  for whānau development.
explanation: A fragment about freeing up resources for whānau development. Purely programmatic resource allocation with no moralized language.

text: We will give 1 weeks paid Parental leave for either parent to take, giving them more choice.
explanation: A paid parental leave policy framed as giving parents 'more choice.' Choice here is a policy benefit, not an explicit ethical concept like fairness, rights, or dignity.

text: Policy alignment will ensure the wise use of public dollars.
explanation: 'Wise use of public dollars' is fiscal prudence/efficiency language, an administrative concern rather than an appeal to ethical standards or virtues.

text: At £1.4 Trillion, that equates to £54,353 per household;
explanation: Purely fiscal arithmetic (debt per household). No normative or moral content.

text: maintain the Defence Forces’ proud reputation in peacekeeping
explanation: 'Maintain the Defence Forces' proud reputation in peacekeeping' deploys the evaluative virtue term 'proud,' appealing to honor and pride — consistent with the codebook's marker of ideals of human virtue (cf. patriotism, courage). Borderline because it is brief, but 'proud' is explicitly evaluative language about honor.

text: The Nationals are determined to eliminate the divide between those living in and those living outside major capital cities, including any limitation on access to a fair legal system that respects the rights and responsibilities of all Australians.
explanation: Contains multiple explicit ethical concepts: a 'fair legal system' and one that 'respects the rights and responsibilities of all Australians.' Fairness and rights are key markers in the clarification.

text: These moves will eliminate remaining inequality in the income tax system and enhance its progressive nature.
explanation: 'Eliminate remaining inequality in the income tax system' invokes equality — a listed ethical concept — as a normative goal to be achieved. Although set in a tax context, 'inequality' is explicitly evaluative and normative.

text: It is now enshrined in law that we must pay 0.7 per cent of our Gross National Income (GNI) on aid every year.
explanation: Describes a legally enshrined requirement to spend 0.7% of GNI on aid. The 'must' denotes a legal obligation being reported descriptively, not a moral exhortation; per the negative clarification, descriptive fiscal/legal commitments are excluded.

text: Caroline Lucas and housing In July 2014 Caroline Lucas MP introduced a Housing (Affordability, Supply and Tenant Protection) Bill to highlight the problems faced by private tenants.
explanation: A descriptive account of Caroline Lucas introducing a housing bill to highlight tenant problems. It reports an action and policy problems without deploying moralized or evaluative ethical language.

text: Support for 2,500 additional aged care beds;
explanation: A programmatic spending commitment for additional aged care beds. No moral terminology.

text: Develop new community policing structures, through local policing forums in individual communities, to reconnect the Gardaí and local communities in a spirit of genuine partnership.
explanation: Community policing reform 'in a spirit of genuine partnership.' Partnership language is administrative-collaborative, not an ethical concept like justice, rights, or dignity.

text: We will: save you money by cutting government waste
explanation: A fiscal promise to save money by cutting government waste. Standard cost-saving rhetoric without moral framing.

text: Ireland should be the best place in the world to grow up, and to grow old.
explanation: 'Ireland should be the best place in the world to grow up, and to grow old' is a generic aspirational commitment to positive societal outcomes. Per the negative clarification, such visions without explicitly moralized or evaluative ethical language (rights, justice, dignity, desert) are coded 0.

text: Ministerial Cars: We will end the automatic entitlement to a State car for every Government Minister.
explanation: An administrative reform ending automatic State car entitlement for ministers. No ethical concepts or moral-duty language are invoked.

text: If you can’t trust Labour and National to go public about poisoned baby milk then what on earth can you trust them on.
explanation: The attack invokes 'trust' — a civic virtue of honesty/integrity — and accuses opponents of a moral failure to be transparent about a public safety matter ('poisoned baby milk'), moralizing the critique. Ambiguous since it also functions as a competence attack, but the appeal to trustworthiness is virtue-laden.

text: All TDs will be entitled to put forward proposals for legislation and a lottery at the start of each session will determine which Bills will be debated.
explanation: A parliamentary procedural reform (lottery to select Bills for debate). Institutional mechanics with no moral language.

text: We will put in train preparations for the 100th anniversary of the Easter Rising, in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week,
explanation: 'In a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week' explicitly invokes honour and patriotic commemoration, matching the codebook's virtue markers (patriotism, ideals of human virtue).

text: We will support sensible immigration policies that meet our economic needs
explanation: Immigration policy framed as 'sensible' and meeting 'economic needs' — utilitarian/economic reasoning, not moral rhetoric.

text: Establishing the right accountability framework for schools.
explanation: Establishing an accountability framework for schools is administrative; 'right' here means appropriate/correct, not moral rights.

text: Republicans share President Bush's understanding that just as events in Europe determined the outcome of the Cold War, events in the broader Middle East will set the course for the victory of free nations in the War on Terror.
explanation: 'Victory of free nations in the War on Terror' invokes freedom as a normative ideal and frames geopolitics as a moral struggle between free nations and terror, going beyond technical or strategic description.

text: • there is appropriate time for debate to be conducted.
explanation: A procedural stipulation about appropriate debate time. No moral content.

text: All recreational fishers should help police the system to ensure that there is no room for poachers and quasi ‘recreational’ fishers who sell or raffle their catches.
explanation: An appeal for recreational fishers to help police the system against poachers. This is regulatory compliance/enforcement language; any civic-duty implication is instrumental and lacks explicit ethical terminology.

text: •  Created  2000 jobs  during the recession  through state housing upgrades.
explanation: An economic achievement claim (jobs created via state housing upgrades). Purely programmatic/descriptive.

text: Constitutional stability for Northern Ireland;
explanation: 'Constitutional stability for Northern Ireland' is an institutional/political goal with no moralized or evaluative language.

text: It will dismantle the dysfunctional Health Service Executive (HSE) that was created by Micheál Martin in 2004,
explanation: 'Dysfunctional' is a performance evaluation of an administrative body, not a moral judgment. The text proposes institutional restructuring without ethical framing.

text: conflicts with long-term strategies to cut waste volumes by recycling and reduction, requires huge scale to operate efficiently and generates large volumes of traffic.
explanation: A technical critique of a waste strategy (scale, efficiency, traffic). No moral or ethical vocabulary.

text: and transition to a prosperous, decarbonized economy.
explanation: A transition to a 'prosperous, decarbonized economy' is an economic/environmental policy goal stated without moralized language.

text: This will support our aim to make Britain the best place in Europe, and one of the top five worldwide, to do business by 2020.
explanation: An aspiration to make Britain a top place to do business — purely economic competitiveness framing.

text: The Nationals believe that, when wealth is generated in a region, a fair share of the resulting government revenue should be returned to that region and to regional Australia more generally.
explanation: 'A fair share of the resulting government revenue should be returned to that region' explicitly invokes fairness and desert (regions deserving revenue by virtue of generating wealth) — key markers in the codebook.

text: Half a million of us regularly play sport, while 400,000 volunteer as coaches, match officials and referees.
explanation: Descriptive statistics on sport participation and volunteering. 'Volunteer' is used descriptively, and no ethical or normative claims are made.

text: We recognise the contribution that Mäori enterprise and entrepreneurship has made to our nation's economy.
explanation: 'We recognise the contribution that Māori enterprise... has made to our nation's economy' is an economic recognition statement without ethical concepts or moral-duty language.

text: We will: Work to secure the full implementation of the Military Covenant in Northern Ireland.
explanation: The 'Military Covenant' denotes a solemn, binding compact of national duty toward service members; invoking it appeals to moral obligation (a codebook marker: statements indicating moral duty). Borderline because the sentence is programmatic in form, but 'covenant' is duty-laden language.

text: abolish the current 2% limit for funding political parties, which acts against new and smaller parties and could be seen as supporting the status quo;
explanation: A critique of the party-funding cap based on its effects on new/smaller parties and the status quo. This is political-strategic reasoning about competition; no explicit ethical terms (e.g., fairness, justice) are used.

text: After so long in office, Mr Howard has forgotten what fairness actually means.
explanation: 'Mr Howard has forgotten what fairness actually means' explicitly deploys the ethical concept of fairness — a listed key marker — to morally indict the opponent.

text: • develop Parents as First Teacher (PAFT) programmes across the country.
explanation: A programmatic commitment to develop parent-education programmes. No moral framing.

text: We will crackdown on overseas producers who don’t cooperate with anti-dumping investigations
explanation: A trade-enforcement pledge to crack down on non-cooperative overseas producers in anti-dumping investigations. Instrumental regulatory language without ethical framing.

text: Labour will ensure that the Defence  Forces are appropriately equipped and staffed to meet Ireland’s  obligations to United Nations and EU peacekeeping missions.
explanation: A commitment to equip and staff the Defence Forces to meet Ireland's obligations to UN and EU peacekeeping missions. 'Obligations' here refers to formal international commitments; the statement is capability/administrative in tone without moralized language.

text: Processing of applications and decision-making is subject to long delays, while the absence of legislation means there is frequent resort to the Courts for judicial review.
explanation: A critique of administrative delays and frequent judicial review due to absent legislation. A technical description of process failings with no moral terminology.
